title: New Insights into the Complexities of Shell Growth and the Strong Influence of Particle Volume in Nonblinking “Giant” Core/Shell Nanocrystal Quantum Dots

paper.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

sections: Bibliographic identity, abstract and graphical abstract; intro literature context. Abstract generalization retained alongside 3 nm exception in main p.9.
Introduction continuation; complete materials list, characterization and single-dot/lifetime acquisition; both equations visually read including square root.
Full core/shell synthetic procedure, core-size variants, Scheme 1 and footnote, all five Table 1 schedules and QYs.
All six Table 2 rows and embedded TEMs, qualitative QY and phase ratios; anneal statistics, inequality and ODE precipitation context.
OD dilution and ligand amounts; all six Figure 1 panels, peak assignments and complete caption; population/sample limits.
Secondary/no-added-amine variants, interpretive surface mechanisms, full withdrawal/OA comparison and start of constant-S procedure.
All four Table 3 rows and TEMs; constant-S outcome, Figure 2 attachment image/caption and dipole mechanism discussion.
Surface termination hypothesis and start-order statement; Figure 3 panels, legends, color/core mapping and caption.
Figure 4, all four color/core series, explicit 3 nm exception; empirical/model distinction and complete conclusion.
SI declaration, notes/acknowledgments and all 23 numbered references including both 8a and 8b; no cited full texts claimed read.
Cover title/byline and full contents list confirming all figures and Table S1.
Contents continuation, all three Figure S1 TEM panels/caption; Figure S2 pure-OA spectrum and all eleven inset band rows.
Figure S3 two morphologies/caption; all five Figure S4 panels and labels 74:26, 67:33, 40:60; caption continuation tracked to S4.
Complete S4 semiquantitative XRD-fit caption; conceptual Figure S5 packing drawing and full interpretation caption.
Both Figure S6 FTIR traces and all printed peak assignments; secondary-amine versus oleylamine/NH2 conflict retained.
All eighteen Table S1 rows and 180 numeric cells, headings, fit expression, normalization and weighted-lifetime equations, complete fitting caveat.
Figure S7 experimental decay/fit, log axis, source-specific 5.5 nm/16.9 ML and acquisition; no forced Table S1 join.
Figure S8 two binary populations and red/blue individual traces, all axis/sample labels and caption continued to S9.
S8 readout/threshold continuation; square-root equation; full hypothetical-volume and actual 7 nm core-only negative-control discussion.

supporting_information.scope: All ten main and nine matched SI pages were read and visually inspected by the extraction author. A distinct source audit of extraction revision 2 passed. Raw fit trajectories and atomic-coordinate files are not supplied or invented.

document_identity_verification.method: Exact source hashes and matching six-author byline/title; main SI declaration and figure/table continuity.

independent_audit: Complete supplied ten-page main article and matched nine-page SI read and independently audited. Separate canonical/reader, molecular and apparatus audits passed. Two routes, three variants, ten supporting procedures and six observation contexts remain distinct. Missing precursor preparations, unresolved specimen joins and source-scoped comparisons are retained. No new training task or exact structure–recipe pair is admitted.
publication_status: Source-reviewed contribution integrated locally; browser and live release tracked separately.

items.title: Compare ODE/OD primary-amine shell conditions and optional late OD dilution
items.text: Compare ODE/OD primary-amine shell conditions and optional late OD dilution. For 3–4 nm cores in ODE/primary amine, precipitation begins after about seven monolayers following Cd addition. Added S/ODE initially redissolves particles; at more than eleven layers an entire sulfur aliquot no longer fully clears the solution. Replacing ODE by OD delays initial turbidity until at least eleven monolayers. Beginning at ten monolayers, modest OD dilution reduces dot concentration and improves size/shape uniformity. Combined with longer annealing, this produces the Table 2 row 3 spherical/faceted population; no complete per-layer dilution schedule is given. Missing fields: complete per-row protocol. This operation groups source-described alternatives for navigation, not a single physical charge containing all alternatives simultaneously.

items.title: Compare primary, secondary and no-added-amine preparations
items.text: Compare primary, secondary and no-added-amine preparations. The described typical shell reaction adds all primary oleylamine initially, while OA enters with each Cd aliquot. An illustrative fourteen-layer context compares 15 mmol amine with 6.5 mmol OA. The medium is approximately equal polar/nonpolar mass; this is not a complete formulation recipe. Dioctylamine suppresses precipitation but gives nonemissive octahedral particles with predominantly wurtzite phase. The proposed eight alternating polar facets and nonpolar overall shape are the authors’ interpretation, not an atomic-coordinate reconstruction. Removing added amine, while allowing residual core-bound primary amine, causes the earliest precipitation from three monolayers. Table 2 separately places hexagonal faceting beyond six monolayers. Missing fields: exact secondary-amine amount, all row batch labels. This operation groups source-described alternatives for navigation, not a single physical charge containing all alternatives simultaneously.

items.title: Supply sulfur for thirteen layers at the beginning; add Cd layerwise with four-hour intervals
items.text: Supply sulfur for thirteen layers at the beginning; add Cd layerwise with four-hour intervals. Charge sulfur sufficient for thirteen monolayers at the start, then add only Cd precursor one monolayer at a time with four-hour intervals. This is a distinct modified SILAR schedule. Turbidity begins at seven layers but remains approximately constant and smaller rather than cycling. QY is low, particles are rods, and XRD gives wurtzite:zinc-blende 40:60. Missing fields: complete initial formulation, exact aliquots.

items.title: Influence of reaction stoichiometry
items.text: The four stoichiometry variants retain both poor and improved outcomes. The 1% and 10% labels denote withdrawal of reaction solution while precursor charges remain fixed; they are not molar excess percentages. The TEM images show moderately thick shells, while the quantum-yield column concerns shells thicker than 15 monolayers. Those observations are not joined as one verified same-thickness specimen.

items.text: The eighteen rows report mean fit coefficients and mean average lifetimes for four core sizes. Amplitude coefficients are normalized, but displayed rounding and averaging need not reproduce exact unity or exact average lifetime from the printed mean coefficients. Initial guesses strongly affect individual components, less the converged mean lifetime.

items.title: Coefficients and lifetimes
items.text: All eighteen rows and 180 numeric values preserve the printed core diameters, TEM-derived shell counts and volumes, amplitudes, component lifetimes and reported average lifetimes. The four core-size families stay separate. Mean and rounded coefficients do not necessarily recompute the reported mean lifetime exactly. The 5.5 nm/16.9 ML trace examples are not forced onto the 15.57 ML row.

sample_scope.link_limit: Core sizes, shell cycles and explicit source contexts are retained. They do not identify one physical batch across microscopy, diffraction, ligand analysis and luminescence.

items.title: Illuminate continuously and acquire CCD time series
items.text: Illuminate continuously and acquire CCD time series. A Coherent Cube continuous-wave diode at 405 nm illuminates the sample. A simple lens gives an approximately circular focal spot. PL passes through a dichroic and spectral filter to a liquid-nitrogen-cooled Princeton Spec-10 CCD. Collect 20,000 frames with 100 ms integration and approximately 90 ms readout while constantly illuminated, giving slightly more than one hour total. SI S8 reports readout as 91 ms. Missing fields: exact power per specimen.

items.title: Classify each dot/frame against background threshold and use ever-emitting population
items.text: Classify each dot/frame against background threshold and use ever-emitting population. Igor Pro groups pixels into dots, averages pixel intensity per dot and frame, and applies I_pix > BG + 2 sqrt(BG). I_pix is not background-subtracted. Below-threshold dots may remain discernible. Statistics use all dots that ever emitted, not every physical deposited particle. Main prose uses greater than 99% on-time over sixty minutes, while Figure 3 uses at least 99%. Retain the printed inequality distinction; denominator is dots that emitted at least once during observation. Missing fields: raw trajectories.

items.title: Acquire TCSPC, fit triexponentials and report mean lifetime
items.text: Acquire TCSPC, fit triexponentials and report mean lifetime. Use PicoQuant LDH-P-C-405B pulsed excitation, wide-field illumination and neutral-density attenuation. The stated optical-power regime is several nW to hundreds of pW, not exact interval endpoints. Collect through a 100×, NA 1.3 oil-immersion objective, dichroic and long-pass filter; use Perkin-Elmer SPCM-AQR-14 SPAD and PicoQuant PicoHarp 300 TCSPC. Igor Pro fits triexponential histograms and computes the reported average lifetime from amplitude and lifetime coefficients. The eighteen rows report mean fit coefficients and mean average lifetimes for four core sizes. Amplitude coefficients are normalized, but displayed rounding and averaging need not reproduce exact unity or exact average lifetime from the printed mean coefficients. Initial guesses strongly affect individual components, less the converged mean lifetime. Missing fields: raw fit files.

figures.label: Nonblinking fractions and volume

The caption uses at least 99% on-time, while main prose elsewhere uses greater than 99%.

remaining_gaps: Cd-oleate and TOP-Se preparation, stock batch volumes, exact dissolved speciation and dioctylamine supplier/grade are absent. CdO and Se/TOP are listed but no unreported precursor preparation reaction is invented.

Exact several-minute/second durations, quench temperature/volume, addition rates, centrifugation settings, washing volumes and yields are absent. The 7 nm and still larger control-core preparation is unreported.

Many TEM/FTIR/XRD population images lack unique batch/core/shell labels. Table series are parameter comparisons, not a complete factorial design. No exact cross-technique or per-row QY/lifetime joins are fabricated.

Precursor aliquot volumes, exact particle number calibration, layer-by-layer concentration/dilution schedule and exact OA switch cycle are absent. One-percent and ten-percent labels are removed solution fractions, not known molar excesses.

Some concentrations/deposition volumes, QY comparison settings, TEM voltage/grid, exact film thickness and numeric dilution factors are unreported; laser spot/power quantities preserve their approximate scope.

TEM and PXRD support morphology and phase associations; no atomic coordinates, full refined cell constants, CIF, SAED or dipole measurement is provided. The 0.3375 nm ML assumption is not a qualified product structure.
FTIR assignments and proposed ligand binding/termination mechanisms do not establish exact ligand counts, coverage, metal complexes or surface atom positions.

Figure 3/4 points and uncertainty bars are not digitized into invented precision. SI S1 reports averages of fitted parameters; original fit/trajectory files, exact uncertainties and individual source records are unavailable. The approximately 750 nm³ relationship and ~65 ns trend remain scoped, with the 3.0 nm exception.

Source, canonical/reader, molecular, apparatus, symbolic product-context and browser audits passed. Public deployment verification is tracked separately. No atomic product model or exact structure–recipe training pair is admitted.

evidence_conflicts.title: Preferred schedule versus comparison schedules
evidence_conflicts.description: Preferred main p.3 anneals S 1 h / Cd 2.5 h; Table 1 has separate S 1 h / Cd 3 h and other schedules. Main p.3 says initial 5–8 cycles then ligand ratio switch; p.6 says more OA starting at the fifth to eighth shell. These are retained as differently worded scopes, without a fabricated exact switch.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

evidence_conflicts.title: Rounded narrative anneal and table QY values
evidence_conflicts.description: Main p.4 calls the long total anneal 3 h although Table 1 asymmetric schedules include 3 h plus 10 min. Narrative 21±0.2% and 41±6% are distinct summaries, while the table uses approximate/bounded QYs; do not replace either set.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

evidence_conflicts.title: SI secondary-amine caption identity
evidence_conflicts.description: Figure S6 specifies dioctylamine synthesis but names oleylamine/NH2 in its thin-shell assignment. Main p.6 describes dioctylamine signatures. No identity correction or quantitative surface-ligand coverage is inferred.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

evidence_conflicts.title: Nonblinking inequality
evidence_conflicts.description: Main p.4 says >99% on-time; Figure 3 says ≥99%. Both remain explicit, with the experimental classification equation and denominator retained.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

evidence_conflicts.title: Approximate versus displayed phase ratio
evidence_conflicts.description: Table 2 gives secondary-amine ~70:30 WZ:ZB; Figure S4c labels 67:33. Primary-amine S4b is 74:26 and constant sulfur S4d 40:60. These are separate source presentations, not substituted values.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

evidence_conflicts.title: Large-core shell-label join remains unverified
evidence_conflicts.description: SI S7 and S8 specify 5.5 nm/16.9 ML; Table S1 ends the 5.5 nm sequence at 15.57 ML. The trace examples are not force-joined to that row. Nominal versus TEM-derived layer counts might differ, but the paper does not explicitly resolve the mapping.
evidence_conflicts.resolution: Retained explicitly; no numerical or identity substitution.

route_evidence_scope_notes.all: The linked records are study context, not a statement that every figure measured the exact product of this route.
route_evidence_scope_notes.core: 3/4 nm common growth, 2.2 nm quench and 5.5 nm feed variants are separate branches. The unreported preparation of 7 nm core-only control is not inherited from them.
route_evidence_scope_notes.shell: The preferred S 1 h/Cd 2.5 h schedule differs from Table 1. Source half-layer precursor additions, full shell cycles and Cd prepassivation remain distinct.
